user.title: AI Workspace
user.description: Shared chat settings. After this, add the first agent (Cursor, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama, and others). Connections and agents are rows on this integration.

data.enable_sidebar: Show AI Workspace in the sidebar

data_description.stt_engine: Browser uses the device speech engine and needs https:// or localhost. A Home Assistant engine (Whisper, and others under Settings) transcribes a recording from this page. The browser still has to allow the microphone, which it only does on https:// or localhost.
data_description.tts_engine: Piper, Google Translate, or an AI Workspace voice from an OpenAI-style agent. Speaking the reply works on plain http://. Off leaves replies as text.
data_description.speak_replies: When a voice is selected, each reply is read as it arrives. Off keeps the speaker button so you can play a reply yourself.
data_description.enable_sidebar: The sidebar item labeled AI Workspace. The page stays available at /ai-workspace if this is off.
data_description.enable_overlay: Turns the floating AI button on or off. On Settings pages it sits higher so it does not cover system buttons.
data_description.allow_users: Signed-in users who are not administrators can open the floating chat. Off keeps it to administrators. The sidebar entry stays administrator-only. They only get the built-in Home Assistant MCP Server with their own permissions.
data_description.house_map: Optional local index for wiring of a named item (triggers, related ids). Off by default. Not for listing automations or on/off — use live MCP for that. Not live state, history, or traces.
data_description.shorten_mcp_results: On by default. Large MCP replies (the whole house, long lists) are shortened before cloud models and Cursor read them. Off sends the full replies. Admins see Last MCP result: unchanged / area-map / truncated after a tool returns.
data_description.change_history: On by default. Records agent configuration writes in Change History for cloud agents and Cursor. Off skips snapshots; the MCP proxy still routes tools and can still shorten results.
data_description.cross_chat: Off by default. When on, a question can use another chat whose title shares words with it. You do not have to mention chat. A short excerpt only, and that chat is not changed.
data_description.keep_chats: Newest unpinned chats to keep per person. Pinned chats are always kept. Default 30.
data_description.runtime_token: Shared secret for a Docker Runtime. Set the same value as RUNTIME_TOKEN on the container. The add-on is paired automatically; leave this empty.

data_description.mcp_kind: Only MCP servers this Home Assistant can reach are listed. Custom is any MCP HTTP URL.
data_description.mcp_token: Built-in: Home Assistant long-lived access token, or leave empty to use your current login in this chat. HA-MCP: usually empty. Vibecode: Agent Key. Custom: optional Bearer token.

data_description.system_prompt: Tone and behavior only. Leave empty for the built-in prompt. MCP tools and editor links are always added; they are not part of this field.

error.no_runtime: The Cursor runtime is not reachable. Start it and set its URL on AI Workspace.
error.invalid_auth: The provider rejected this API key.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the provider. Check the URL and the network.

user.title: Connection
user.description: Only MCP servers this Home Assistant can reach are listed. Custom is any MCP HTTP URL.

connection.title: Connection
connection.description: An MCP server the assistant can use in the same chat.

data_description.name: A short name, such as Directus. The assistant uses it to tell this connection from the others.
data_description.url: The MCP address, starting with https:// or http://. Found servers are filled in.
data_description.token: Only if that server asks for a key. Leave empty when editing to keep the saved key.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: Choose the provider. The next screen asks only for what that provider needs.

data_description.api_provider: Cursor, or a cloud or local model.

provider_cursor.title: Cursor
provider_cursor.description: Cursor API key, model, and effort. The runtime URL stays on AI Workspace.

data_description.cursor_api_key: From cursor.com/dashboard/integrations. Leave blank when editing to keep the saved key. Leave empty when the Runtime already has CURSOR_API_KEY.
data_description.model: Pick one or type an id. Empty uses Composer.
data_description.effort: Fast, High, or High fast. Composer uses Fast unless you pick High.
data_description.assist: Adds this agent to Home Assistant Assist. Off keeps it in the AI Workspace chat only and removes the Assist pipeline this agent added.

provider_cloud.title: Cloud agent
provider_cloud.description: This agent keeps its own key. Copy one from an integration that is already set up, or paste a new one. Leave the key blank when editing to keep the saved key.

data_description.borrow: Uses the key already stored by that integration. The other integration is left as it is.
data_description.model: Pick one or type an id. Empty uses the provider default.
data_description.effort: Fast, High, or High fast when the model supports it.
data_description.low_token: A short prompt and no tools, so a small model can answer. It cannot check or change the house.
data_description.check_house: The first step of every message (except greetings and thanks) must call a tool, so answers about the house come from live data. Turn it off for models that call tools reliably on their own, or to save a tool round on general questions.
data_description.assist: Adds this agent to Home Assistant Assist. Off keeps it in the AI Workspace chat only and removes the Assist pipeline this agent added.
data_description.assist_stt: Uses this agent's API key as a Home Assistant Speech-to-text engine and assigns it to every AI Workspace Assist pipeline (including Cursor). Off removes the Speech-to-text engine this agent added.
data_description.stt_model: Empty uses the provider default. Whisper is cheaper; gpt-4o-mini-transcribe is the OpenAI default. You can type another id.
data_description.assist_tts: Uses this agent's API key as a Home Assistant Text-to-speech engine and assigns it to every AI Workspace Assist pipeline (including Cursor). Off removes the Text-to-speech engine this agent added.
data_description.tts_model: Empty uses gpt-4o-mini-tts. tts-1 is cheaper. You can type another id.
data_description.tts_voice: Coral is the default. The same voices speak German, French, and the other languages you pick under Assist → Language. Assist pipelines this agent created use this voice.
data_description.tts_speed: How fast this voice speaks. 1× is normal. Applies to AI Workspace and Assist.

provider_ollama.description: Point this at the Ollama server.
